Latest insights for July and August
21.09.2026
Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remained severely constrained throughout July and August, with no evidence of a broad or durable recovery. Activity continued to vary significantly across cargo segments. Outbound crude oil, LNG, and fertilizer-related shipments showed only brief and uneven activity around late June and early July, and the rebound was not sustained in the weeks that followed. Agricultural inbound shipments showed more persistent activity into August, though volumes remained volatile and well below normal levels.

Strategic trade insights: Cross-commodity impacts in July and August

 

The analysis below is based on vessels visible through AIS. Shipments by vessels not transmitting AIS are not captured in the charts.

 

July and August data indicate that shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz remained highly restricted and uneven across cargo categories. The temporary improvement seen around late June and early July did not develop into a sustained recovery. Seven-day moving averages for crude oil, LNG, and fertilizer-related outbound shipments remained close to zero for most of the two-month period, while agricultural inbound shipments showed more persistent, but still volatile, activity.

 

Crude oil outbound shipments to destinations outside the Persian Gulf recorded a brief pickup in late June and early July, with several shipments temporarily lifting the seven-day moving average. However, activity declined rapidly during July and returned to near-zero levels by mid-month. Only isolated shipments were visible around the end of July, early August, and again in mid-August. These sporadic movements were insufficient to generate a sustained increase in the moving average, which remained close to zero through most of August. This indicates that regular AIS-visible crude oil outbound activity through the Strait had still not resumed by the end of the month.

 

LNG outbound shipments experienced an even more limited recovery. A small number of shipments in late June and early July briefly lifted the seven-day moving average, but the increase was short-lived. No meaningful LNG shipment activity was observed from early August onward. As a result, the seven-day moving average remained near zero for the rest of the month, indicating that regular LNG outbound shipments through the Strait remained effectively suspended.
